nsSection.heading: Nutri-Score Distribution
nsSection.body: None of the {{total}} analysed ice creams receive Nutri-Score A. Only one product receives B. The majority ({{nsDECount}} products, {{nsDEPct}}%) are in category D or E. This means that ice cream as a food category is one where "healthy" is a relative concept — the best options are those with the least sugar and saturated fat.

novaSection.heading: NOVA Groups
novaSection.calloutHeading: All {{total}} ice creams are NOVA 4 — ultra-processed products.
novaSection.calloutBody: NOVA 4 means the product contains industrial ingredients not available in a regular kitchen — emulsifiers, stabilisers, flavourings, colourings. This classification, regardless of sugar or fat content, indicates a high degree of processing. Ice cream is by definition an industrial product, so NOVA 4 is no surprise — but it is important to know when choosing food products for children.

top10LowSugar.heading: TOP 10: Lowest sugar per 100 g
top10LowSugar.tableDesc: Ice creams with the lowest sugar per 100 g
top10LowSugar.note: Products with the least sugar are often unsweetened or contain artificial sweeteners. Check the ingredient list before choosing.

top10LowSatFat.heading: TOP 10: Lowest saturated fat per 100 g
top10LowSatFat.tableDesc: Ice creams with the lowest saturated fat content
top10LowSatFat.note: Saturated fat mainly comes from cream and coconut oil. Frozen juice bars and sorbet usually contain significantly less saturated fat than traditional cream ice cream.

top10FewAdditives.heading: TOP 10: Fewest concerning additives
top10FewAdditives.tableDesc: Ice creams with the fewest Limit + Caution + Avoid additives
top10FewAdditives.note: The count includes ingredients classified as "Limit", "Caution", or "Avoid" from the ingredient analysis database — the same number shown on product cards. Products without ingredient analysis data are not included.

highValues.heading: Highest values — use in moderation
highValues.desc: These products are not the "worst" — but they contain the highest values of sugar, fat, or additives. Use this information to make an informed choice.

methodology.heading: About the data
methodology.body: The analysis includes {{total}} ice creams from Rimi and Maxima (Barbora) in the categories "Portion ice creams", "Large package ice creams", and "Frozen juice bars". Data sourced from the ABCDE.lv database, which regularly updates information from Rimi.lv and Barbora.lv. Nutritional values are given per 100 g of product. Nutri-Score and NOVA groups are calculated according to European standard methodology. The additive count reflects the number of "Limit", "Caution", and "Avoid" ingredients from the ABCDE.lv ingredient analysis — the same number shown on product cards.
